name: CMH Protect Kit
author: codemasterhub

sections.description:
CMH Protect Kit gives WordPress site owners practical, local tools for reducing unwanted copying, dragging, and reuse of published content. It combines content protection controls, image watermarking, protected-content access rules, and visitor-facing message styling in one focused admin interface.

Use CMH Protect Kit to apply protection to selected WordPress views, posts, pages, media, and public post types. You can choose the visitor roles that should receive protection, keep forms and editors usable with safety exclusions, and customize the messages shown when a protected action is blocked.

Key features include:

  • Text selection and clipboard protection for copy, cut, paste, and select-all actions.
  • Mouse protection for right-click and drag actions.
  • Targeting for standard WordPress views, public post types, and selected visitor roles.
  • Safety exclusions for super admins, form fields, editors, and custom CSS selectors.
  • Image watermarking with image or text marks, built-in watermark images, opacity controls, sizing, positioning, and margins.
  • Server-side uploaded-image watermark delivery with image type matching and image CSS selector exclusions.
  • Protected content access rules for content placed inside the [cmhpk_block] shortcode.
  • Unlock options for shortcode-protected content, including custom message, password, and login access.
  • Customizable alert messages, positions, colors, typography, spacing, borders, and preview controls.
  • Import and export tools for moving or backing up plugin settings.

The plugin stores settings locally in WordPress and does not require a CodeMaster Hub account or license key. An optional Pro add-on is available for sites that need separate visitor blocking, activity logging, advanced targeting, and managed update modules.

Upgrade: CMH Protect Kit Pro
Support: CodeMaster Hub Support
Documentation: CMH Protect Kit Documentation

Requirements

CMH Protect Kit is a standalone plugin and does not require another plugin.

Free Features

  • Text selection and clipboard protection for copy, cut, paste, and select-all actions.
  • Basic mouse protection for right-click and drag actions.
  • Server-side image watermark settings with built-in image marks or text marks in a single placement.
  • Watermark image type matching and image CSS selector exclusions.
  • Protected content rules for content placed inside the [cmhpk_block] shortcode.
  • Message, password, and login access options for shortcode-protected content.
  • Message and alert styles.
  • Targeting for standard WordPress views and public post types.

For advanced content access rules, URL targeting and exclusions, advanced browser shortcut controls, custom watermark images, repeated watermark layouts, visitor blocking, activity logs, and managed Pro updates, view CMH Protect Kit Pro.

Privacy

CMH Protect Kit stores plugin settings in the WordPress database. The free plugin does not transmit visitor activity, protected content, or site settings to CodeMaster Hub.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the cmh-protect-kit folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate CMH Protect Kit from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open CMH Protect Kit in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Configure the protection modules you want to enable.
  5. Save your settings and test the protected pages in a private browser window.
sections.faq:
Does CMH Protect Kit require a CodeMaster Hub account?

No. The free plugin works without a CodeMaster Hub account or license key.

Does this plugin guarantee that protected content can never be copied?

No browser-based protection plugin can provide an absolute guarantee. CMH Protect Kit adds practical deterrents and access controls, but determined users may still find ways to capture visible content.

Can I protect custom post types?

Yes. The free plugin can target public post types registered on your site.

Does the free plugin send data to CodeMaster Hub?

No. The free plugin stores its settings locally in WordPress and does not send site data to CodeMaster Hub.
